messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: Dedicated pool us-east-1-reserved-A at 100% GPU utilization; queue depth 53; affected tenants: Pelican Insights, Meridian Analytics. Autoscaler retried and hit provider rate limits.

emma: ack. paging @raj (on-call SRE) and @jen (infra lead).

raj: looking now. queue jumped +30 over 6m. GPU util 99%; gpu-node-7 showing high fragmented device memory.

jen: autoscaler shows 429s from cloud API: "rate limit: instance launches per minute exceeded" plus intermittent 502 on init scripts.

alex: runtime telemetry points to Pelican batch KV-cache allocations that pin large chunks of GPU memory. Their jobs launched concurrently due to a cron overlap.

rom_support: CS reporting Pelican customer-facing latency spikes; customers seeing 5-12s enqueued. I raised a support ticket and asked Pelican to pause non-critical jobs — they can't immediately.

ana_cs: Pelican compliance team says they cannot stop the scheduled runs; asked for options without tenant intervention.

raj: mitigation options:
- enable pool-level preemption of best-effort workloads temporarily
- migrate Meridian Analytics (non-reserved) to us-east-1-burst fallback
- attempt manual warm provisioning of 2 GPUs in burst pool (subject to provider rate limits)
- drain problematic node if memory fragmentation persists

jen: initiating manual provision. Provider still returning rate-limit; estimated acceptance 8-12m per API message.

alex: we have a policy flag allowing preemption of best-effort pods in reserved pools but it's off by default. Recommend enabling for short window.

sre-lead: we can flip the flag but need product + security signoff due to SLA implications. @leah and @mike-sec please weigh in.

leah: product ok for a temporary 25m window if CS communicates impact. prefer short window only.

mike-sec: security ok provided we don't move customer data and only evict best-effort jobs. approve 25m.

emma: jen, flip preemption. raj, prepare eviction dry-run and command.

jen: preemption flag set=true for pool us-east-1-reserved-A

raj: dry-run candidates:

```
redwoodctl pool list-candidates --pool us-east-1-reserved-A --strategy best-effort
# candidates: be-4421, be-4427, be-4492 (approx 3.5GB GPU each)
```

raj: executing eviction for be-4421, be-4427

raj: evictions successful. GPU util dropped to 72%, queue from 53 -> 11.

incident-bot: NOTE: Auto-rollback timer scheduled in 25m; will revert preemption flag at 1889013845 unless extended.

rom_support: Pelican notified. They acknowledged but noted throughput reduction for some internal analytics workflows.

ana_cs: opening follow-up w/ Pelican about reservation sizing and isolation (recommend dedicated tenant allocation or stricter batch limits).

alex: node gpu-node-7 still logs OOMs intermittently:

```
2026-07-21T09:18:32Z gpu-node-7 kernel: Out of memory: kill process 8891 (pclient-infer)
2026-07-21T09:18:33Z runtime: kvcache: eviction failed: pinned
```

raj: marking gpu-node-7 for drain, shifting shards. initiating drain now.

jen: drain started; moving 4 shards to warm nodes. provider accepted new nodes; ETA ~5m.

emma: interim summary:
- root cause: synchronized large KV-cache batch jobs from Pelican + provider launch rate limits
- mitigations: enabled preemption to evict best-effort, attempted manual provisioning, drained fragmented node
- impact: Pelican experienced increased latency; Meridian migrated to burst pool

leah: action items: policy to prevent unbounded KV pinning on shared reserved pools; consider guardrails on batch concurrency and tenant-specific soft reservations.

mike-sec: will work with policy owner to update wording; capture tenant IDs and timestamps for compliance record.

raj: final check: GPU util 60%, queue 0, autoscaler healthy; no 429s in last 6m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Stabilized. Postmortem assigned to @raj, @jen, @leah. Severity lowered to SEV2. Closing paging.

emma: thanks all. monitoring for 30m then postmortem writeup.

ana_cs: following up with Pelican CS on capacity options.

raj: collecting logs and timeline; will draft postmortem.

emma: closing thread. :white_check_mark:
